metadata.title: Data Structures Quiz: Binary Search Trees
metadata.instructions: Choose the correct answer for each question. This quiz assesses your understanding and application of Binary Search Trees.

questions.question_text: What is the primary advantage of using a Binary Search Tree (BST) over a simple sorted array for searching?
questions.answer_key: The primary advantage is that BSTs allow for efficient insertion and deletion of elements, whereas in a sorted array, these operations can be costly.
questions.notes: Source: General academic knowledge of data structures

questions.question_text: Analyze the time complexity of searching, inserting, and deleting a node in a balanced Binary Search Tree. How do these operations compare in terms of efficiency?
questions.answer_key: Searching, inserting, and deleting a node in a balanced BST each have an average time complexity of O(log n), making them equally efficient in terms of time complexity.
questions.notes: Assumes knowledge of Big O notation and basic operations on BSTs

questions.question_text: Consider a scenario where you need to frequently search for and insert new elements into a dataset. Would you prefer using a Binary Search Tree or a hash table? Justify your choice.
questions.answer_key: A Binary Search Tree would be preferred because it allows for both efficient search (O(log n)) and insertion (O(log n)) operations, whereas a hash table, while excellent for search (O(1) average), may have variable performance for insertion depending on the load factor and collision resolution strategy.
questions.notes: Requires understanding of trade-offs between data structures
